--- title: "Schools that win more produce more draftees, strongly in the Power conferences and moderately in the Group of 5" date: "2026-10-31" description: "From 2013 to 2025, a school's win percentage tracked its draft rate with a correlation of 0.82 among Power schools and 0.40 in the Group of 5." followups: - "Does recruited talent drive both winning and drafting? Add team recruiting ratings at entry as a common cause." - "Do head coaches carry draft production with them when they change schools?" - "Season by season, does a winning season come before or after a rise in a school's draft class?" - "Do draftees from programs that produce above expectation also last longer in the NFL?" author: - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco" freeze: auto vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Schools that win more produce more draftees, strongly in the Power conferences and moderately in the Group of 5} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} *Data as of the latest published release, retrieved 2026-10-31. Records cover FBS seasons 2010 through 2025; players are counted in their final college season, 2013 through 2025, which covers approximately the draft classes of 2014 through 2026.* ::: ## 1. Introduction The [first post](2026-10-31-conferences-landscape.html) found draft picks concentrated in a short list of schools, and the [second](2026-10-31-who-produces-draftees.html) found Power-conference players drafted at five times the Group of 5 rate. This post asks whether the schools that win, like Joe Burrow's 15-0 LSU of 2019 or Jordan Travis's 13-1 Florida State of 2023, are the schools whose players get drafted. + *Expectation: teams that win more produce more draftees.* ## 2. Data ### 2.1 Each of 137 FBS schools has a winning percentage and a draft rate The table defines every term; the 137 FBS schools (65 Power, 72 Group of 5) played 25,666 FBS-season games from 2010 to 2025 and had 36,199 eligible players, 3,044 of them drafted, in final seasons 2013 to 2025. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Term , ~Meaning , "FBS" , "The Football Bowl Subdivision, the top division of college football." , "School" , "An FBS program with at least one player whose college career ended there in a Power or Group of 5 season from 2013 to 2025." , "Tier" , "Power (the SEC, Big Ten, ACC, Big 12, the Pac-12 through 2023, the Big East through 2012, and Notre Dame) or Group of 5 (the American Athletic, Conference USA, Mid-American, Mountain West, Sun Belt, the Western Athletic through 2012, the two-school Pac-12 of 2024 and 2025, and the other independents). Counts and draft rates by tier place each player in the tier of their final season, as in the previous post. Comparisons between schools place each school in the tier it held in most of its FBS seasons from 2010 to 2025, so Cincinnati, which joined the Big 12 in 2023, is Group of 5." , "Win %" , "Wins divided by completed games over all of a school's FBS seasons from 2010 to 2025, bowls and playoffs included. A school that wins six of every ten games has a win % of 60%." , "SP+" , "A rating of how strong a team was in a season that adjusts each game for the opponent's strength, so a win over a strong team counts for more than a win over a weak one; higher is better. A school's SP+ is the average over its FBS seasons from 2010 to 2025." , "Eligible player" , "A player whose college career ended at the school and who had a real shot at the NFL: at least three seasons on college rosters, or drafted, or signed with an NFL team undrafted (the same definition as the previous post)." , "Draft rate" , "Drafted players divided by eligible players, counting each player once, for the last school they played for, in final seasons 2013 to 2025." , "Correlation (r)" , "How closely two numbers rise and fall together across schools, on a scale where 0 means no relationship and 1 means the schools sit on a perfect rising line. The plausible range shows how far r could move by chance with this few schools: the span the true correlation likely falls in (a 95% confidence interval)." , "Expected draftees" , "For a school with this record in its tier, how many draftees we would expect: a curve fitted to the schools of each tier turns a win % into an expected draft rate, which is multiplied by the school's eligible players. The curve is a logistic regression, chosen because its expected rates stay between 0% and 100%." , "Over- or under-producer", "A school with more (over) or fewer (under) draftees than expected for its record." , "Transfer-in" , "An eligible player who was on a different school's roster in an earlier season before finishing at the school that gets the credit." ) |> kable(caption = "Terms used throughout.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Terms used throughout. |Term |Meaning | |:-----------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |FBS |The Football Bowl Subdivision, the top division of college football. | |School |An FBS program with at least one player whose college career ended there in a Power or Group of 5 season from 2013 to 2025. | |Tier |Power (the SEC, Big Ten, ACC, Big 12, the Pac-12 through 2023, the Big East through 2012, and Notre Dame) or Group of 5 (the American Athletic, Conference USA, Mid-American, Mountain West, Sun Belt, the Western Athletic through 2012, the two-school Pac-12 of 2024 and 2025, and the other independents). Counts and draft rates by tier place each player in the tier of their final season, as in the previous post. Comparisons between schools place each school in the tier it held in most of its FBS seasons from 2010 to 2025, so Cincinnati, which joined the Big 12 in 2023, is Group of 5. | |Win % |Wins divided by completed games over all of a school's FBS seasons from 2010 to 2025, bowls and playoffs included. A school that wins six of every ten games has a win % of 60%. | |SP+ |A rating of how strong a team was in a season that adjusts each game for the opponent's strength, so a win over a strong team counts for more than a win over a weak one; higher is better. A school's SP+ is the average over its FBS seasons from 2010 to 2025. | |Eligible player |A player whose college career ended at the school and who had a real shot at the NFL: at least three seasons on college rosters, or drafted, or signed with an NFL team undrafted (the same definition as the previous post). | |Draft rate |Drafted players divided by eligible players, counting each player once, for the last school they played for, in final seasons 2013 to 2025. | |Correlation (r) |How closely two numbers rise and fall together across schools, on a scale where 0 means no relationship and 1 means the schools sit on a perfect rising line. The plausible range shows how far r could move by chance with this few schools: the span the true correlation likely falls in (a 95% confidence interval). | |Expected draftees |For a school with this record in its tier, how many draftees we would expect: a curve fitted to the schools of each tier turns a win % into an expected draft rate, which is multiplied by the school's eligible players. The curve is a logistic regression, chosen because its expected rates stay between 0% and 100%. | |Over- or under-producer |A school with more (over) or fewer (under) draftees than expected for its record. | |Transfer-in |An eligible player who was on a different school's roster in an earlier season before finishing at the school that gets the credit. | ::: ::: ## 3. Results ### 3.1 Within each tier, schools that win more have higher draft rates *Expectation: teams that win more produce more draftees.* ✅ Win % tracks draft rate closely for Power schools (r = 0.82) and moderately for the Group of 5 (0.40), where small schools new to FBS pull the correlation down, such as James Madison with 78% wins and 0 of 72 eligible players drafted. The tiers sit on separate curves: at 60% wins, a Power school is expected to see 14.2% of its eligible players drafted and a Group of 5 school 3.9%. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} win_cor |> left_join(tier_tot, by = "tier") |> left_join(wtd_cor, by = "tier") |> mutate(at60 = at60[as.character(tier)]) |> transmute( Tier = tier, Schools = schools, `Eligible players` = fmt(eligible), Drafted = fmt(drafted), `Draft rate` = pct(draft_rate), `Correlation of win % with draft rate (r)` = r2(r), `Plausible range of r` = paste(r2(lo), "to", r2(hi)), `r, each school weighted by its eligible players` = r2(r_wtd), `Expected draft rate at a 60% win %` = pct(at60) ) |> kable( caption = "School win % (FBS seasons 2010 to 2025) against draft rate (final seasons 2013 to 2025), by tier. Eligible players and draftees are counted in the tier of their final season; the correlations and fitted curves group schools by the tier they held in most seasons, and the weighted correlation lets schools with more eligible players count for more." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: School win % (FBS seasons 2010 to 2025) against draft rate (final seasons 2013 to 2025), by tier. Eligible players and draftees are counted in the tier of their final season; the correlations and fitted curves group schools by the tier they held in most seasons, and the weighted correlation lets schools with more eligible players count for more. |Tier | Schools|Eligible players |Drafted |Draft rate |Correlation of win % with draft rate (r) |Plausible range of r |r, each school weighted by its eligible players |Expected draft rate at a 60% win % | |:----------|-------:|:----------------|:-------|:----------|:----------------------------------------|:--------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------| |Power | 65|18,610 |2,561 |13.8% |0.82 |0.73 to 0.89 |0.83 |14.2% | |Group of 5 | 72|17,589 |483 |2.7% |0.40 |0.19 to 0.58 |0.49 |3.9% | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} grid <- school |> group_by(tier) |> reframe(win_pct = seq(min(win_pct), max(win_pct), length.out = 100)) |> group_by(tier) |> mutate( fit = predict( win_fits[[as.character(first(tier))]], newdata = pick(everything()), type = "response" ) ) |> ungroup() p <- ggplot(school, aes(win_pct, draft_rate, color = tier)) + geom_point_interactive( aes( tooltip = paste0( team, " (", tier, "): ", pct(win_pct), " wins, ", pct(draft_rate), " drafted" ), data_id = team ), size = 3.4, alpha = 0.55 ) + geom_line(data = grid, aes(y = fit), linewidth = 1.6) + annotate( "segment", x = 0.6, xend = 0.6, y = at60[["Group of 5"]], yend = at60[["Power"]], color = "#111827", linewidth = 1.1, arrow = arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(0.25, "cm")) ) + # labels in the empty upper left, tied to the curve values at 60% annotate( "segment", x = 0.45, xend = 0.595, y = c(0.31, 0.26), yend = c(at60[["Power"]], at60[["Group of 5"]]), color = c(tier_colors[["Power"]], "#b45309"), linewidth = 0.7 ) + annotate( "label", x = 0.45, y = c(0.31, 0.26), label = c( paste0("Power school at 60% wins: ", pct(at60[["Power"]]), " expected"), paste0("Group of 5 school at 60% wins: ", pct(at60[["Group of 5"]]), " expected") ), hjust = 1, size = 5, fontface = "bold", color = c(tier_colors[["Power"]], "#b45309"), linewidth = 0 ) + scale_color_manual(values = tier_colors, name = NULL) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + labs( x = "Win % (FBS seasons 2010 to 2025)", y = "Draft rate", title = "Draft rate rises with win % in both tiers, on separate curves", subtitle = sprintf( "Each dot is a school; lines are each tier's fitted curve (r = %s Power, %s Group of 5)", r2(wc("Power", "r")), r2(wc("Group of 5", "r")) ) ) + theme_cfb2nfl() girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 8) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tip <- function(d) { paste0( d$team, " (", d$tier, ")\nRecord 2010 to 2025: ", d$record_label, " (", pct(d$win_pct), "); average SP+ ", fmt(d$sp, 1), "\n", d$drafted, " drafted of ", d$eligible, " eligible (", pct(d$draft_rate), "); ", fmt(d$expected, 1), " expected" ) } school$tip <- tip(school) p <- ggplot(school, aes(win_pct, draft_rate)) + geom_line( data = grid, aes(y = fit), color = "#9ca3af", linewidth = 1.2 ) + geom_point_interactive( aes(fill = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = team), shape = 21, size = 4.2, color = "white", stroke = 0.6 ) + facet_wrap(~tier, scales = "free_y") + scale_fill_team(teams, guide = "none") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + labs( x = "Win % (FBS seasons 2010 to 2025)", y = "Draft rate", title = "Every FBS school's record and draft rate", subtitle = "Team colors; each panel has its own vertical scale; hover a dot for the record, SP+ and counts" ) + theme_cfb2nfl() girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 8) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### 3.2 Florida and LSU produced 34 and 28 more draftees than their records predict, and Oklahoma State and Kansas State 23 and 22 fewer The table and bars rank each tier's five schools furthest above and below their expected draftees: LSU, where Burrow finished after starting at Ohio State, is second among Power schools, while Alabama's record already predicts so many draftees that it sits at +15.8. In the Group of 5, Cincinnati leads, and the three service academies sit among the four schools furthest under. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bind_rows(over, under) |> arrange(tier, desc(above)) |> transmute( Tier = tier, School = team, `Record 2010 to 2025` = record_label, `Win %` = pct(win_pct), `Eligible players` = eligible, Drafted = drafted, Expected = fmt(expected, 1), `Drafted minus expected` = signed(above, 1) ) |> kable( caption = "The five schools in each tier with the most draftees above and below the number expected for their record, final seasons 2013 to 2025." ) ``` ::: ``` ::: ::: ### 3.3 SP+, which adjusts for opponents, tracks draft rate more closely than win %, most of all in the Group of 5 Replacing win % with SP+ raises the correlation from 0.82 to 0.87 for Power schools and from 0.40 to 0.61 for the Group of 5, as the table and scatter show. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} win_cor |> select(tier, schools, r_win = r) |> left_join(select(sp_cor, tier, r_sp = r, lo, hi), by = "tier") |> left_join(win_sp, by = "tier") |> transmute( Tier = tier, Schools = schools, `r, win % with draft rate` = r2(r_win), `r, SP+ with draft rate` = r2(r_sp), `Plausible range, SP+` = paste(r2(lo), "to", r2(hi)), `r, win % with SP+` = r2(r_win_sp) ) |> kable( caption = "Correlations with school draft rate (final seasons 2013 to 2025) of win % and of average SP+ (FBS seasons 2010 to 2025), by tier, and of the two measures with each other." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Correlations with school draft rate (final seasons 2013 to 2025) of win % and of ``` ::: ::: ### 3.4 A Power school's draft rate carries over from one five-year window to the next Across the 65 Power schools, the draft rate of final seasons 2013 to 2017 correlates 0.68 with that of 2019 to 2023. Early win % tracks later draft rate about as closely as early draft rate tracks later win % (0.57 each), so the data cannot say which comes first. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} window_cor |> transmute(`Earlier window with later window` = measure, r = r2(r)) |> kable( caption = "Correlations across the 65 Power schools between an earlier window (2013 to 2017) and a later one (2019 to 2023), leaving 2018 out so no player's final season falls in both windows, though players from the later window's first years were on rosters during the earlier one. Win % uses FBS seasons in each window; draft rate uses final seasons in it." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Correlations across the 65 Power schools between an earlier window (2013 to 2017) and a later one (2019 to 2023), leaving 2018 out so no player's final season falls in both windows, though players from the later window's first years were on rosters during the earlier one. Win % uses FBS seasons in each window; draft rate uses final seasons in it. |Earlier window with later window |r | |:----------------------------------------------------|:----| |Draft rate 2013 to 2017 with draft rate 2019 to 2023 |0.68 | |Win % 2013 to 2017 with win % 2019 to 2023 |0.61 | |Win % 2013 to 2017 with draft rate 2019 to 2023 |0.57 | |Draft rate 2013 to 2017 with win % 2019 to 2023 |0.57 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lim <- c(0, max(c(windows$rate_a, windows$rate_b)) * 1.05) p <- ggplot(windows, aes(rate_a, rate_b)) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#6b7280") + geom_point_interactive( data = filter(windows, !team %in% movers$team), aes( tooltip = paste0( team, ": ", pct(rate_a), " drafted in 2013 to 2017, ", pct(rate_b), " in 2019 to 2023" ), data_id = team ), size = 3.6, color = "#9ca3af" ) + geom_point_interactive( data = movers, aes( fill = team, tooltip = paste0( team, ": ", pct(rate_a), " drafted in 2013 to 2017, ", pct(rate_b), " in 2019 to 2023" ), data_id = team ), shape = 21, size = 5.5, color = "#111827" ) + # hand-placed labels: Penn State below a neighbouring dot, Arkansas # above and Louisville below their near-identical points geom_label( data = mutate( movers, lx = rate_a + c(0.012, 0, 0.012, 0.012), ly = rate_b + c(0, -0.025, 0.015, -0.015), hj = c(0, 0.5, 0, 0) ), aes( lx, ly, label = paste0(team, " ", signed(100 * change), " percentage points"), color = team, hjust = hj ), size = 4.8, fontface = "bold", linewidth = 0 ) + annotate( "text", x = lim[2], y = 0.005, label = sprintf("r = %s; above the dashed line, the rate rose", r2(wr[1])), hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5, fontface = "bold", color = "#374151" ) + scale_fill_team(teams, guide = "none") + scale_color_team(teams, guide = "none") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + coord_equal(xlim = lim, ylim = lim) + labs( x = "Draft rate, final seasons 2013 to 2017", y = "Draft rate, final seasons 2019 to 2023", title = "Power schools mostly keep their draft rate", subtitle = "The two largest rises and falls in team colors" ) + theme_cfb2nfl() girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 11, height_svg = 9) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} slopes <- windows |> mutate( team = reorder(team, rate_b), tip = paste0( team, "\n2013 to 2017: ", drafted_a, " drafted of ", eligible_a, " (", pct(rate_a), "), win % ", pct(win_a), "\n2019 to 2023: ", drafted_b, " drafted of ", eligible_b, " (", pct(rate_b), "), win % ", pct(win_b) ) ) p <- ggplot(slopes, aes(y = team)) + geom_segment( aes(x = rate_a, xend = rate_b, yend = team), color = "#9ca3af", linewidth = 1.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm")) ) + geom_point_interactive( aes(x = rate_a, tooltip = tip, data_id = team), size = 2.8, color = "#9ca3af" ) + geom_point_interactive( aes(x = rate_b, fill = team, tooltip = tip, data_id = team), shape = 21, size = 3.8, color = "white" ) + scale_fill_team(teams, guide = "none") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + labs( x = "Draft rate", y = NULL, title = "Every Power school's draft rate, 2013 to 2017 to 2019 to 2023", subtitle = "Grey dot: earlier window; colored dot: later window; hover for counts and win %" ) + theme_cfb2nfl(base_size = 13) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 11, height_svg = 15) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### 3.5 Leaving out transfer-ins barely changes how closely win % tracks draft rate Without transfer-ins (Burrow, Cam Ward and Jordan Travis among them, but not Josh Allen, on Wyoming rosters only), the correlation with win % is 0.82 for Power schools and 0.36 for the Group of 5. That holds even though Power transfer-in draftees grew from at most 10 a class through 2019 to 113 of 237 in the class of 2026. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} transfer_tier |> left_join(select(win_cor, credit_tier = tier, r_all = r), by = "credit_tier") |> left_join(select(home_cor, credit_tier = tier, r_home = r), by = "credit_tier") |> transmute( Tier = credit_tier, `Eligible players` = fmt(eligible), `Transfer-ins among them` = paste0(fmt(eligible_tin), " (", pct(eligible_tin / eligible, 0), ")"), Drafted = fmt(drafted), `Transfer-ins among draftees` = paste0(fmt(drafted_tin), " (", pct(drafted_tin / drafted, 0), ")"), `r, win % with draft rate` = r2(r_all), `r, without transfer-ins` = r2(r_home) ) |> kable( caption = "Transfer-ins and the win % correlation with and without them, by tier, final seasons 2013 to 2025. Discussion ::: {.callout-important} Winning and drafting rise together, but this data cannot say which drives which. - Early winning tracks later drafting about as closely as early drafting tracks later winning (0.57 each, Power schools). - Recruited talent may drive both, since the players a school signs shape both its record and its draft class; testing that needs recruiting ratings at entry. ::: ::: {.callout-important} Schools with similar records can differ widely in draftees. - Oklahoma State won 65% of its games and had 25 of 282 eligible players drafted; Florida won 58% and had 72 of 287. - The three service academies are among the four Group of 5 schools furthest below expectation, likely because their graduates owe military service. ::: A school's tier is the one it held most often, so Cincinnati, Houston, UCF, BYU and SMU count as Group of 5 despite their Power seasons, and the totals of the Group of 5 over-producers Cincinnati, Houston and UCF include seasons after their move to the Big 12. Schools scatter around the fitted curves more than chance alone would produce, so expected draftees are a benchmark rather than a forecast. Transfer-ins are detected only through rosters, which start in 2010 and grow from 227 schools in 2021 to 307 in 2022.
